title: Anthropic's AI broke Git (Thu 12 Nov off day; rewritten and redrawn 13 Nov, words approved by Krish 13 Nov)

five_whys.a: Git became its biggest bottleneck, in Anthropic's own words.

five_whys.q: Why did Git become the bottleneck?
five_whys.a: Code changes went from about 2,500 a day in May to over 30,000 by September.
Its AI now writes most of the code, all day and all night.

five_whys.q: Why does that matter beyond programmers?
five_whys.a: When AI does the work, the hold-up moves to the people who check it: Faros AI found 21% more work done but 91% longer waits for review.

five_whys.q: Why should a business person care?
five_whys.a: Every business has human-speed checks (sign-offs, approvals, legal, the boss's inbox) that will jam the same way unless checks are set by risk.

explains.git: where every programmer saves their work, like track changes for code (card 1)

cards.headline: Anthropic's AI broke Git.
cards.line: Git is where every programmer saves their work, like track changes for code.
cards.picture: The robot arm in a storm of paper over a filing cabinet, the Anthropic logo

cards.headline: 12x more code in four months.
cards.line: Code changes saved per day at Anthropic.
cards.picture: Two bars to scale: 2,500 in May, 30,000+ in September

cards.headline: Git was built for human speed.
cards.line: People save their work a few times a day. AI saves changes all day and all night.
cards.picture: Code changes piling up at a narrow funnel marked GIT

cards.headline: So Anthropic built one for AI.
cards.line: 7 engineers, 5 months. It's called Scion. Anthropic's AI, Claude, wrote most of its code.

cards.headline: But the jam moved to people.
cards.line: The hold-up is now the people who check the AI's work.
cards.picture: Two bars: work finished +21%, time waiting for a person to check it +91%
cards.source: Faros AI, The AI Productivity Paradox, 2025 (teams of 10,000+ developers)

cards.headline: Doing got faster. Checking didn't.
cards.line: So the company as a whole shipped no faster.
cards.picture: A robot handing work to one person behind a tall pile
cards.source: Faros AI, 2025: delivery metrics stayed flat

cards.headline: Your business has this jam coming.
cards.line: Any step where AI's work waits for a person to say yes.
cards.picture: Four in-trays stacking: sign-offs, approvals, legal checks, the boss's inbox

cards.headline: Check by risk, not habit.
cards.line: Not every piece of work needs the same human check.
cards.picture: Low risk: AI checks, a person spot-checks. High risk (money, customers, the law): a person signs off

cards.headline: Find what waits for a human.
cards.line: That's your new traffic jam. Fix it before AI floods it. Follow for more.
cards.picture: A WAITING ON YOU sign, Follow for more over the centred wordmark

read_back.reader: Fresh reader A (Haiku, a small-business owner, headlines only, once)

answers.what: A carousel about Anthropic's AI and Git, the tool programmers use to save their work.
answers.happened: Anthropic's AI made about 12 times more code in four months, overloading Git, so Anthropic built a version for AI.
answers.why: Writing got much faster but checking did not, so the slow part moved to people.
answers.so_what: My business may get the same jam: work arrives faster than people can check it.
answers.do: Find the work that waits for a human and check it by risk, not habit.

read_back.reader: Fresh reader B (Sonnet, a 15-year-old, headlines only, once)

answers.what: A company's AI messing up a thing programmers use to save their work.
answers.happened: The AI wrote way more code, the old saving tool could not keep up, so they made a new one.
answers.why: The old tool was made for slow humans, not fast AI.
answers.so_what: Work piles up when people have to check things.
answers.do: Check by risk and find what waits for a human, if you run a business.
